key_insight: An LLM agent uses physics-based simulations to inverse-design fabrication recipes for desired depth profiles of implanted ions or vacancies.
engineering_relevance: The approach could help translate spatial material designs into ion-processing recipes for graded materials, metamaterials, and quantum superlattices.
method: Specify a target ion or vacancy depth profile.
Let the agent select ion species, energies, incident angles, and target material layers.
Run and interpret ion–matter simulations, then iteratively refine the recipe.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based matching of target profiles with minimal human input, but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics or experimental validation.
watch_item: Practical fabrication requires validating simulated profiles against experiments and equipment constraints.
paper_title: Agentic inverse design of spatially programmed materials
